title: Potential smooth equivariant cover of an almost homogeneous scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian integrally closed domain of Krull dimension one with finitely many maximal ideals [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $G\to S$ be a separated flat group scheme of finite type, and $X\to S$ a separated flat scheme of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. A group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group identities; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $G$ acts on $X$ and $X$ is a finite union of invariant open subschemes $X_j$ for which $G\times_S X_j\to X_j\times_S X_j$, $(g,x)\mapsto(gx,x)$, is surjective as an fppf sheaf morphism [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-fppf-site]. Then there exist a finite field extension $L/K$, the integral closure $R'$ of $R$ in $L$ (the elements of $L$ satisfying monic polynomials over $R$), $T=\operatorname{Spec}R'$, a smooth separated finite-type $T$-group scheme $H$ with geometrically connected fibres (for every field $\Omega$ and every morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ the fibre $H_\Omega=H\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is connected), and a smooth separated finite-type $T$-scheme $Y$ with an $H$-action [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. The ring $R'$ is again a Noetherian integrally closed domain of dimension one with finitely many maximal ideals. There is a $T$-morphism $Y\to X\times_ST$ whose composite $q:Y\to X$ is integral, surjective and has finite underlying fibres [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For every algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, the fibre $Y_\Omega$ is a finite disjoint union of open $H_\Omega$-orbits: each nonempty piece is open and any two of its points with values in any algebraically closed extension of $\Omega$ are related by an element of $H$ over that extension. Empty $X$, empty fibres and pieces with only generic support are allowed. No commutativity, excellence, smoothness of $G$ or $X$, or finiteness of $R'$ as an $R$-module is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.3 (OCR 4,2,5), printed pp.58–59, conclusions (i),(ii) and proof; Appendix II Corollaries 2 and 3, printed p.73: finite normalization after a finite fraction-field extension. Take the neutral component of the smooth normalized group; the proof identifies its geometric orbits with the connected components of the smooth normalized space. Krull–Akizuki for the semilocal integral closure; the projection to X is a finite normalization followed by an integral base change, not asserted finite over X. Local archive WANTED; primary scan read at https://www.numdam.org/article/MSMF_1973__33__5_0.pdf

proof.text: The finite-type generic fibres of $G$ and $X$ are Noetherian and have finitely many irreducible components. Apply [lem-pur-finite-inseparable-geometric-reduction] to their disjoint union to choose a finite purely inseparable $K_0/K$ for which both reduced generic fibres are geometrically reduced. Put $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}R_0$, with $R_0$ the integral closure of $R$ in $K_0$. By [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres], $R_0$ is Dedekind and $S_0\to S$ is surjective with finite fibres and finite residue extensions. Each maximal ideal of $R_0$ lies over one of the finitely many maximal ideals of $R$ (integrality); hence $R_0$ is semilocal. Its localizations at maximal ideals are DVRs by [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr].

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 p.58, initial finite radicial extension; Stacks 04KT and 09IG for the generic reduction and base normalization.

proof.text: Write $G_0=(G_{S_0})_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $Z_0=(X_{S_0})_{\mathrm{red}}$. They are separated finite type. They remain flat: locally on each DVR, the original affine algebra $B$ is torsion free by flatness. If $ab$ is nilpotent with nonzero base element $a$, then $a^nb^n=0$ implies $b^n=0$; thus $B/\sqrt0$ is torsion free and therefore flat by [lem-weil-pbc-pid-torsion-free-module-flat] and the affine criterion. A flat affine algebra over a domain embeds in its generic localization; consequently a flat scheme with reduced generic fibre is reduced. This applies also to products of $G_0$ and $Z_0$: their affine tensor algebras are flat (tensoring two flat modules preserves injections successively), and their generic fibres are reduced by geometric reducedness. Hence multiplication, inverse, identity and the action factor uniquely through the reductions by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme]. The diagrams hold after the closed immersions, so define a group $G_0$ acting on $Z_0$. The same reducedness argument remains valid after further normalized finite base extension.

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 p.58, reduced flat models and restriction of the action; Stacks 0356 for factorization into reductions.

proof.text: For every algebraically closed field over $S_0$, the reduced models have the same field-valued points as the original base changes, by [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism]. The given fppf-surjectivity therefore implies transitivity on each nonempty inherited open piece: the fibre of the action relation over a pair is a nonempty finite-type scheme over that algebraically closed field, so a maximal ideal in a nonzero affine chart gives a rational point by [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma]. This also works after any algebraically closed extension. Invariant open pieces with a common geometric point are the same orbit; discard repetitions, obtaining finitely many disjoint open orbits. In particular this conclusion holds on the generic fibre. The geometrically reduced generic group $(G_0)_{K_0}$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth]. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-equivariant-open-orbits] with $P=Q=(G_0)_{K_0}$, $V=W=(Z_0)_{K_0}$ and both finite maps the identities. It gives smoothness of $(Z_0)_{K_0}$. Thus both generic fibres are geometrically normal by [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal].

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 p.58, smooth generic fibres and fibrewise almost homogeneity; Milne 1.65–1.66 for the field orbit argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semitrait-potential-reduced-normalization] to the two schemes $G_0,Z_0$ over $S_0$. Obtain a finite extension $L/K_0$, its normalized base $T$, and finite surjective normalization maps $A\to G_{0,T}$ and $B\to Z_{0,T}$; $A,B$ are normal, flat, separated and finite type over $T$, with geometrically reduced fibres and generic-fibre normalization maps isomorphisms. The ring of $T$ is also the integral closure $R'$ of $R$ in $L$: integrality is transitive (finitely many coefficients of a monic equation lie in a finite $R$-module subalgebra, which together with the element is again finite), while an equation over $R$ is also one over $R_0$. The finite extension $L/K$ therefore has the required normalized semilocal Dedekind base by [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres], exactly as in step 1. Both models are locally of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation].

source.place: Appendix II Corollary 2 p.73, applied simultaneously; Prop.4.2.3 pp.58–59, normalized models.

proof.text: Cover the semilocal one-dimensional normal base $T$ by its open traits $T_{\mathfrak m}=\operatorname{Spec}R'_{\mathfrak m}$: this is the complement of the other closed points, and distinct such opens meet in $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Apply [lem-sfb-trait-normalization-group-structure] on every trait to $G_{0,T}$ and its normalization $A$. The model $G_{0,T}$ is already reduced by step 2; its generic fibre is smooth, and the finite normalization $A$ is flat with geometrically reduced special fibre by step 4. All hypotheses of that node hold. Its unique group laws agree on overlaps because the generic normalization is the identity. Glue them by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing], obtaining a group structure on $A$ and a finite surjective homomorphism $A\to G_{0,T}$. Every field-valued fibre of $A$ is a geometrically reduced finite-type group and hence smooth by [lem-sfb-geometrically-reduced-group-smooth]. Flatness and local finite presentation from step 4 give smoothness of $A/T$ by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion].

source.place: Appendix II Corollary 3 p.73 and Prop.4.2.3 pp.58–59, smooth normalized group; trait-local gluing gives the semilocal case.

proof.text: Let $Z=Z_{0,T}$. Via $A\to G_{0,T}$, $A$ acts on $Z$. Both the projection $\pi:A\times_TZ\to Z$ and the action $a:A\times_TZ\to Z$ are smooth: $a$ is projection after the isomorphism $(g,z)\mapsto(g,gz)$ with inverse $(g,z)\mapsto(g,g^{-1}z)$, and $\pi$ is a base change of $A/T$. Apply [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-smooth-pullback] first to $\pi$ and then to $a$. It identifies $(A\times_TZ)^\nu$ with $A\times_TB$ over $A\times_TZ$, and its projection to $B$ using $a$ defines the lifted action $A\times_TB\to B$. This is equivariant for $B\to Z$. The action diagrams hold generically, where both normalizations are isomorphisms, and hence globally by [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated]. Indeed $B$ is separated over $T$, and every source in the diagrams is flat over $T$ (products of the flat models); on affine charts the injection into generic localization proves scheme-theoretic density. Thus $B$ carries an actual $A$-action, without choosing an orbit or a point.

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 p.59, extension of the action to the normalization; Stacks 035R/normalization and smooth base change, using the existing canonical normalization-pullback node. Milne Lemma 1.64 gives the projection/action isomorphism.

proof.text: For any field $k$ over $T$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-equivariant-open-orbits] to $P=A_k$, $Q=(G_{0,T})_k$, $V=B_k$ and $W=Z_k$. The two maps are finite surjective by step 4 and base change, the first is a group homomorphism by step 5, and equivariance is step 6. The source $B_k$ is geometrically reduced by step 4, $A_k$ is smooth by step 5, and $Z_k$ has the required open geometric orbits by step 3. The lemma gives smoothness of $B_k$ and identifies its geometric connected components with the open orbits of $A_k^0$. Since $B/T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] now proves that $Y=B$ is smooth over $T$. It was already separated and finite type.

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 p.59, geometric orbits of the normalized group and smoothness of the normalized space.

proof.text: On each open trait of step 5 take the subgroup supplied by [lem-sfb-smooth-group-relative-neutral-open] for $A$. The subgroups agree over $\operatorname{Spec}L$ because that node commutes with field base change and specifies the identity component; equivalently their underlying opens are the fibrewise identity components. Glue these opens and the restricted group maps to obtain an open subgroup $H\subseteq A$. The same node ensures that every field fibre of $H$ is geometrically connected and every geometric fibre is the identity component of the corresponding fibre of $A$. The scheme $A$ is Noetherian (finite type over $T$), so [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-immersion-qc] makes $H\to A$ quasi-compact; it is locally of finite type and hence finite type. It is separated as an open subscheme of $A$, and smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. Restrict the action on $Y$ to $H$. Step 7 now gives exactly the requested finite disjoint union of open $H$-orbits, including transitivity after all algebraically closed extensions.

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 pp.58–59, passage to the neutral open subgroup; existing trait-neutral-component theorem, glued over the semilocal base.

proof.text: Define $Y\to X_T$ as $B\to Z_{0,T}\to X_T$. The latter arrow is the base change of the reduction $Z_0\hookrightarrow X_{S_0}$, so is a surjective closed immersion. The former arrow is finite surjective. Thus $Y\to X_T$ is finite surjective (affine-locally a finite module over a quotient is finite over the original ring), in particular integral. The map $X_T\to X$ is integral: it is obtained by tensoring the integral extension $R\subseteq R'$ with each affine $R$-algebra, using [lem-weil-pbc-integral-base-change]. Their composite $q$ is integral by [lem-trf-integral-morphism-composition] and surjective because $T\to S$ is surjective, and a fibre remains nonempty after extending a residue field (tensor with a field extension is faithfully flat). This proves all the required morphism clauses except finiteness of the underlying fibres.

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 and its use in 4.2.2, pp.57–59; Appendix II Corollary 2, finite normalization followed by integral base change.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ over $s\in S$. By [lem-sc-integral-closure-dedekind-surjective-fibres], there are finitely many $t\in T$ over $s$, and each $\kappa(t)/\kappa(s)$ is finite. The fibre $(X_T)_x$ has underlying points in the finite union of $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(x)\otimes_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t))$. Each displayed algebra is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(x)$ and hence has finitely many prime ideals: descending chains of ideals terminate, every prime quotient is an Artinian domain and thus a field, and distinct maximal ideals give independent nonzero factors, bounded by vector-space dimension. Each point of $(X_T)_x$ has finitely many inverse images in $Y$, by finiteness of $Y\to X_T$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Therefore $q^{-1}(x)$ is finite. These constructions also work for empty $X$, empty fibres, or components supported only over the generic point: reduction, normalization and the field lemma allow the empty scheme, and the flatness arguments never assert a nonempty special fibre. No module-finiteness of $R'/R$ has been used.

source.place: Prop.4.2.3 pp.58–59 and integral-cover use in 4.2.2; Krull–Akizuki finite residue extensions rather than module-finiteness of the normalized base.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-f2a6ed241 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 10 steps, both new nodes and all 32 cited statements in full. Source checked in the Numdam scan of Anantharaman, Mém. SMF 33: Prop. 4.2.3 (OCR 4,2,5), pp.58–59, and App. II Thm 1/Cor. 2–3, p.73. The steps follow the source's route: radicial K0, reduced flat models with group law and action, normalization after a finite extension, lifted action, orbits equal to components, written out in detail. Hypotheses checked per step: torsion-free reductions are flat and reduced and products have reduced generic fibres (step 2); fppf-surjectivity gives transitivity on geometric points via Zariski's lemma (step 3); the base T is the integral closure of R in L and the T_m are open (steps 4–5); every hypothesis of trait-normalization-group-structure holds; the action lifts through smooth-pullback normalization and the identities extend by separated density (step 6); every hypothesis of the field node holds in step 7; the relative neutral open glues over the generic point (step 8); integral, surjective and finite-fibre arguments for q are correct (steps 9–10). New node finite-equivariant-open-orbits is true: proved by the dimension count and Milne's orbit lemma; tested on empty V, P=Q, finite P and non-reduced Q; it is a field-level lemma used twice and does not restate the item. New node semitrait-potential-reduced-normalization is App. II Cor. 2 applied to the disjoint union, with no hidden excellence; the extra conclusions follow from finiteness and normality. No duplicates among complete-trait-normalized-reduced-fibres, trait-group-finite-smooth-cover, geonormal-normalization-field-extension and fpqc-finite-presentation-normalization-model. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal, lem-trf-integral-morphism-composition, and the trf section-component nodes under lem-sfb-smooth-group-relative-neutral-open are generic algebraic geometry, not steps of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, and the closure has no PD node or target, so all are accepted. The worker's own 24 tool_uses are all generic and accepted. Minor: step 2 does not name the flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback node in its text; citations.json is absent. No changes made.
